## 🎯 The task

Forecast **your series from Week 4** with ARIMA, as the *ARIMA Models, Part 1* lecture defines it:

- differencing, including **one seasonal difference** if the tests ask for it;
- a **non-seasonal** ARMA($p$, $q$) on the differenced series;
- optionally a log transformation, if the seasonal swing grows with the level;
- **no seasonal AR or MA terms**: $P = Q = 0$. Those are the *Part 2* lecture and Lab 7.

The order matters, and it is marked: **difference, read, specify by hand** — and only then compare with
`AutoARIMA`.

No ETS, no regression, no averaging with other methods.

::: {.callout-important}
## This one counts

8 points. **Deadline: 23:59 today**, on Moodle. Marks and comments come back before the next practice
session.
:::

## Why accuracy is not marked this week — and is again in Lab 7

Every series in the pool was issued only if a **seasonal** `AutoARIMA` beats its benchmark. This week's
models have no seasonal AR or MA terms, so that guarantee does not cover them. Measured on the whole
pool, with exactly this lab's rules:

| Result against your benchmark | Share of the pool | Points it would earn |
|---|---:|---:|
| beat it | 58–60% | 3 |
| within 10% | 24–26% | 2 |
| worse | 16% | 1 |
| full seasonal `AutoARIMA`, for comparison | 100% beat it | 3 |

Whether you lose a point here depends mostly on **how strong the seasonal autocorrelation in your
series is** — the practice session's gas example — not on how well you work. So this week the points go
to the differencing, the specification and the argument. The score is still published: it is the
number Lab 7, with seasonal terms, will be compared against.
:::

## 📊 Section 1 — EDA and visualisation (1 point)

You know this series by now. The plots this week have one job: to justify the **differencing** and the
**transformation** before any model is fitted.

- A time plot, read for trend, season, and whether the seasonal swing grows with the level. If it grows,
  that is your case for `log=True` — ARIMA has no multiplicative season, and the log is how it gets one.
- The validation split on a plot: history, validation window, your chosen model's forecast and 80%
  interval over it.
- One sentence per plot. **A plot with no reading attached earns nothing.**

## 📐 Section 2 — Model and forecast (3 points)

| Item | Points | What earns them |
|------|------:|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 2.1 | 1 | **Differencing.** `difference_plan` with `M` from the setup cell, on $y$ or $\log y$ as Section 1 argued; the differenced series plotted. Overriding a test is allowed and must be argued in 3.1. |
| 2.2 | 1 | **Specification and comparison.** ACF and PACF of the differenced series out to lag $3m$; **at least two hand-specified candidates** written down from that reading; `AutoARIMA` added; all compared with `compare` and decided with `rolling_mase`, the benchmark in the same table. |
| 2.3 | 1 | **The submission.** The chosen candidate refitted on the **whole** history, $h$ steps, with the model's 80% interval, written to the file by the notebook. |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Where this goes wrong

- **Fitting outside `fit_arima`.** It is the only builder in the template, and it refuses seasonal AR and
  MA terms. `AutoARIMA(season_length=M)` on its own will add them — that model is Lab 7's.
- **Comparing AICc across different $d$, $D$ or log choices.** AICc is comparable only between models
  fitted to the same differenced data. Across those choices, `rolling_mase` decides.
- **Ljung-Box with `model_df=0`.** The template's `compare` uses $p + q$ — use the same if you test by
  hand.
- **Reading the residual spike at lag $m$ as a mistake.** With $P = Q = 0$ it is often expected: the
  seasonal difference over-corrects. Report it in 3.3; Lab 7 is where it gets fixed.
- **Forecasting from `train`.** The submission is refitted on the whole history.

📖 [FPP3 §9.1–9.8](https://otexts.com/fpp3/arima.html) ·
[FPP3 §5.10 cross-validation](https://otexts.com/fpp3/tscv.html) ·
[FPP the Pythonic Way, ch. 9](https://otexts.com/fpppy/nbs/09-arima.html)
:::

## ✍️ Section 3 — Justification block (3 points)

The part a human reads closely. Roughly a paragraph each, with numbers from your own cells.

| Item | Points | What earns them |
|------|------:|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 3.1 | 1 | **The differencing.** $D$, $d$ and the log decision, each tied to a test or a plot. If you overrode a test, why — and what the ACF of the result looked like. |
| 3.2 | 1 | **The hand reading and the machine.** The lags in the ACF and PACF that named your candidates; what `AutoARIMA` chose and why it agrees or disagrees with you; the candidate you submitted and the rolling-origin evidence for it. |
| 3.3 | 1 | **What is left, and what you expect.** Ljung-Box with $p + q$ degrees of freedom, read; the residual autocorrelation at lag $m$ and what it says about $P = Q = 0$; your expected skill against the benchmark, and how this model compares with your Lab 5 ETS on the validation window. |

::: {.callout-important}
Marked on the reasoning. A hand specification that `AutoARIMA` beats, with a clear account of why, scores
full marks. So does a series where the honest answer is a random walk — if the ACF of the differences
is what you show for it.
:::
